unitKey: 2Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of stateChemistry

questions.question: What is the relationship between the boiling point and the condensing point of a pure substance?
options: They are the exact same temperature.
The boiling point is always higher than the condensing point.
The condensing point is always higher than the boiling point.
They are unrelated and always occur at different temperatures.

questions.question: What happens to the volume of a substance when it is boiled and enters the gas state?
options: Its volume increases.
Its volume decreases.
Its volume remains exactly the same.
Its volume decreases to zero.

questions.question: How do the distance and movement of particles change when a substance is boiled compared to when it is condensed?
options: Particles move further apart when boiled and closer together when condensed.
Particles move closer together when boiled and further apart when condensed.
Particles grow larger when boiled and shrink when condensed.
Particles stop moving when boiled and vibrate faster when condensed.

questions.question: When using a Bunsen burner, what is the effect of opening the air hole?
options: The flame changes from orange and sooty to a hotter, cleaner blue flame.
The flame goes out completely to ensure laboratory safety.
The flame becomes much larger but stays orange and cooler.
The flame turns into a bright yellow, highly smoking flame.

questions.question: What is the safe and correct way to carry a lit splint in a laboratory setting?
options: Angled slightly downwards and shielded by your other hand.
Held straight up in the air as high as possible.
Pointed directly forward at eye level.
Waved gently back and forth to keep it burning.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the energy states of matter?
options: Solid states have the least energy, while gas states have the most energy.
Liquid states have the least energy, while solid states have the most energy.
Gas states have the least energy, while solid states have the most energy.
All states of matter contain the exact same amount of energy.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the evaporation of a substance in its liquid state?
options: It must reach its boiling point before any evaporation can occur.
It can evaporate at temperatures below its boiling point.
It can only evaporate if the liquid is heated to exactly 100°C.
It can only evaporate when it is cooled to its freezing point.

questions.question: How do the melting point and freezing point of a pure substance compare to each other?
options: They are the exact same temperature.
The melting point is always higher than the freezing point.
The freezing point is always higher than the melting point.
They are completely different and independent temperatures.

questions.question: What keeps the particles of a substance in fixed positions when it is in the solid state?
options: Forces of attraction between the particles hold them in place.
The high pressure exerted by the surrounding atmosphere.
The lack of any heat energy within the individual atoms.
Magnetic forces that only exist at extremely low temperatures.

questions.question: How does the strength of the forces of attraction between particles affect a substance's melting point?
options: The stronger the force of attraction, the higher the melting point.
The stronger the force of attraction, the lower the melting point.
The strength of the forces has no influence on the melting point.
Stronger forces of attraction mean the substance can never melt.

questions.question: What are the approximate temperatures for the freezing point of water, normal room temperature, and average body temperature?
options: 0ºC, 20ºC, and 37ºC respectively
0ºC, 37ºC, and 100ºC respectively
10ºC, 20ºC, and 37ºC respectively
-5ºC, 25ºC, and 40ºC respectively

questions.question: Which set of properties correctly describes a substance in its gas state?
options: It can flow, fills the whole of a container, and can be compressed.
It has a fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed.
It has a fixed volume, does not flow, but can be easily compressed.

questions.question: What is present in the empty spaces between the individual particles in a gas?
options: Air molecules
A thin layer of liquid
Nothing at all
Tiny heat waves

questions.question: Which of the following describes the properties of a substance in its solid state?
options: It has a fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, has a flexible shape, and can be compressed.
It fills the entire container, flows, and can be compressed.
It takes the shape of the container, does not flow, and can be compressed.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the behavior and properties of a liquid state?
options: It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed.
It has a fixed shape, cannot flow, and can be easily compressed.
It can flow, fills the entire container, and can be easily compressed.
It cannot flow, does not have a fixed shape, and cannot be compressed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the particles that make up all substances?
options: They are too small to be seen.
They can be observed easily using a standard school magnifying glass.
They are only present in gases, as solids are made of continuous matter.
They are large enough to see with the naked eye under bright light.
